blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim hypersensitivity contraindication
stem: A client has a documented immediate hypersensitivity reaction to a sulfonamide antibiotic. A new prescription for sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim is entered. Which nursing action is most appropriate?

options.A: Hold the medication and clarify the prescription because known hypersensitivity to trimethoprim or sulfonamides is a labeled contraindication.
options.B: Give a reduced first dose and observe closely because lowering the dose removes the contraindication created by prior hypersensitivity.
options.C: Premedicate with an antihistamine and administer the full dose because premedication overrides the labeled hypersensitivity contraindication.
options.D: Administer the prescribed dose if vital signs are stable because prior sulfonamide hypersensitivity does not affect later use of this medication.

rationale: Current sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim labeling lists known hypersensitivity to trimethoprim or sulfonamides as a contraindication. Therefore A is the appropriate nursing safety action. B does not remove a hypersensitivity contraindication, C uses unsupported premedication to bypass a contraindication, and D ignores the documented allergy risk.
educational_objective: Identify documented hypersensitivity to trimethoprim or sulfonamides as a contraindication to sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim and clarify the prescription before administration.

candidate_reasons_resolved: Rebuilt all options as parallel medication-safety actions of comparable length.
Anchored the keyed action directly to current DailyMed contraindication language.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely follows the labeled contraindication. Dose reduction, antihistamine premedication, or stable vital signs do not negate documented hypersensitivity.
